title: Subtree Inversion Sum
summary: Given an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by edges, and an integer array nums with values at each node, you can invert nodes' values by multiplying them by -1.
statement: Given an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by edges, and an integer array nums with values at each node, you can invert nodes' values by multiplying them by -1. Inversions must follow a distance constraint: if two nodes are inverted, their least common ancestor must be at least k edges away. The goal is to maximize the sum of the tree's node values after applying these operations.
constraints: edges form a tree rooted at zero with up to 50,000 nodes; k <= 50.
Inverting a node flips every value in its rooted subtree. Ancestor-descendant inversion nodes must be at least k edges apart.
Choose inversion nodes to maximize the final total value sum.
hints: A subtree value’s sign is the parity of selected ancestors, while legality depends only on capped distance to the closest selected ancestor.
Root the tree and compute bottom-up DP for sign parity and distance states.
Compare keeping the node with selecting it when distance=k; selection flips parity for children and resets their distance to one.
Children are independent given these two state variables, which capture every effect an ancestor choice can have on a descendant.
